name: Couchbase Capella
tagline: Couchbase's managed DBaaS: Couchbase Server clusters plus App Services sync and AI tooling.
description: Couchbase Capella is the fully managed form of Couchbase Server on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Couchbase runs the clusters, upgrades and backups, and you keep SQL++, the memory-first key-value path, full-text and vector search, and XDCR. Capella adds App Services, which syncs data to Couchbase Lite on mobile and edge devices, plus Capella Analytics for columnar analysis and Capella iQ for AI-assisted query writing. New operational clusters run Couchbase Server 8.0.3 as of September 2026. It suits teams that want Couchbase's latency and offline-sync story without operating a multi-service cluster themselves.

pricing.notes: Free-tier operational cluster for development; paid clusters billed hourly by node size, with credits or committed contracts.

scale.notes: Clusters scale to 50 nodes on GCP and Azure (more on request); XDCR links clusters across regions and clouds.

strengths: Couchbase's memory-first latency without running the cluster yourself
App Services provides managed sync to Couchbase Lite for offline-first apps
Available on all three major clouds with XDCR between them
Customer-managed keys, private networking and fine-grained RBAC
weaknesses: Pricing is opaque compared with per-request serverless databases
No true serverless or scale-to-zero option for operational clusters
Smaller ecosystem of integrations than Atlas or the hyperscaler services
useCases: Managed backends for mobile apps with offline sync
Low-latency profile, session and catalog stores
notIdealFor: Hobby projects that outgrow the free tier but have tiny budgets
Teams that need to run on-premises (use Couchbase Server)
